feed.title: NPR Topics: Politics
feed.subtitle: Follow NPR Politics for nonpartisan coverage of government, elections, policy debates and voting rights. Plus weekday audio from The NPR Politics Podcast.

entry.title: California sues OpenAI over hacking risks
entry.summary: The state's attorney general started investigating OpenAI after the Hugging Face attack and now says this attack was "entirely foreseeable" due to OpenAI's poor security practices.

entry.title: U.S. tightens controls on remote access to AI technology amid Nvidia fallout
entry.summary: The new rule closes a loophole that existed that allowed Chinese companies to still access advanced AI chips remotely, despite U.S. restrictions on their physical sale to China.

entry.title: U.N. talks seek to rein in 'killer robots' as fears over AI weapons grow
entry.summary: Countries are meeting in Geneva to negotiate rules on weapons that can select and kill targets without human intervention. But with the U.S., Russia and Israel resisting legally binding controls, campaigners fear the window to act is closing.

entry.title: Nearly two million people are behind bars in the US. How did we get here?
entry.summary:
Lynn Novick's new, four-part PBS documentary series, Crime and Punishment in America, goes inside the U.S. prison system and explores how
our approach to criminals has changed over time.

entry.title: Lindsay Clancy to face a new trial in spring of 2027 over children's killing
entry.summary: A new trial is set in Massachusetts against Lindsay Clancy as prosecutors seek a criminal conviction over the killing of her three young children.

entry.title: FAA ground stop still affecting thousands of flights. And, Trump meets Xi, Putin in Asia
entry.summary: U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said that things could be back to normal at the end of Monday after an FAA ground stop disrupted flights. And, Trump heads to Asia for a high-profile trilateral summit.

entry.title: Chris Van Hollen says he can beat Chuck Schumer. Here's his case
entry.summary: Sen. Chris Van Hollen told NPR's Morning Edition why he believes he can defeat Sen. Chuck Schumer and what he would change about Senate Democratic leadership.

entry.title: Regulating AI will being a top priority for congressional Democrats in the new year
entry.summary: A big priority for the incoming Congress will be regulating artificial intelligence. Democrats will face stiff opposition from the Trump administration and its hands-off policy towards AI.

entry.title: Trump heads to Asia to meet with Xi and Putin amid Nvidia fallout
entry.summary: The trip to China marks Trump's second time this year, and comes as the president and his party faced widespread backlash from voters in the recent midterm elections.

entry.title: Affordability was a key issue for midterm voters. It helped make childcare one, too
entry.summary: Childcare costs have surged, putting a major financial burden on U.S. families. Advocates say the subject once on the fringes of political debate became a major issue during the midterms.
